people.name: George Berkeley
people.bio: Irish philosopher of immaterialism and Anglican bishop of Cloyne.

stops.note: Entered Trinity College aged 15, after schooling at Kilkenny College.
Fellow of Trinity College; held the position until 1724, interrupted by a four-year European tour as a tutor.
Waited three years for funding for his planned Bermuda college.
Had moved to Oxford to supervise his son's education.

people.name: Leonty Magnitsky
people.bio: Russian mathematics teacher, author of the textbook Arithmetic (1703) used at Peter the Great's navigation school.

stops.note: Appointed teacher in 1701; head of the school from 1715.

people.name: George Frideric Handel
people.bio: German-born composer of operas and oratorios who settled in London.

stops.note: Enrolled at the university in 1702 and was organist of the Reformed Schlosskirche.
Violinist and harpsichordist at the Hamburg opera; first operas.
Study journey in Italy: Florence, Rome, Venice and Naples.
Settled in London after the success of Rinaldo (1711); naturalized 1726.

people.name: Friedrich Wilhelm Zachow
people.bio: German organist and composer at the Marienkirche in Halle, Handel's teacher.

people.name: Ludvig Holberg
people.bio: Norwegian-Danish playwright, historian and professor at Copenhagen.

stops.note: Journey through France and Italy, including Paris and Rome.
Professor of metaphysics 1717, eloquence 1720, history 1730; university quaestor 1737.

people.name: Voltaire
people.bio: French writer and philosopher, the leading figure of the Enlightenment.

stops.note: Exile in England after the Rohan quarrel and a spell in the Bastille.
Lived with Émilie du Châtelet at her estate, away from Paris after the Lettres philosophiques.
At the court of Frederick II in Berlin and Potsdam.
Lived at Les Délices near Geneva.
Settled at his estate of Ferney on the French side of the Genevan border.

people.name: Tiberius Hemsterhuis
people.bio: Dutch classical philologist who founded the Dutch school of Greek studies.

stops.note: Theology, then mathematics under Johann Bernoulli.
Professor of mathematics and philosophy at the Athenaeum Illustre.
Professor of Greek from 1717 (not 1704: until then he taught in Amsterdam); also history from 1738.

people.name: Jacobus Perizonius
people.bio: Dutch classical scholar, professor at Franeker and Leiden.

people.name: Edmond Halley
people.bio: English astronomer and mathematician, Savilian professor and Astronomer Royal, who predicted the return of the comet named after him.

stops.note: Exact date and year somewhat uncertain.
Queen's College; left without examination to observe from St Helena, degree granted 1678.

people.name: John Flamsteed
people.bio: English astronomer, the first Astronomer Royal at Greenwich.

people.name: Christian Wolff
people.bio: German rationalist philosopher and mathematician who systematized Leibnizian philosophy.

stops.note: Magister examination 1702 and habilitation 1703; then lectured as Privatdozent.
Professor of mathematics (inaugural lecture early 1707), lecturing on philosophy from about 1710; expelled by royal edict in November 1723.

people.name: Leonhard Euler
people.bio: Swiss mathematician, the most prolific of the 18th century, who worked at the St Petersburg and Berlin academies.

stops.note: Academy of Sciences: professor of physics 1730, senior professor of mathematics 1733.
Director of mathematics at the Berlin Academy from 1744.
Returned to the St Petersburg Academy.

people.name: Francis Hutcheson
people.bio: Irish-Scottish moral philosopher of the moral sense, professor at Glasgow.

stops.note: Founded and ran a private academy in Dublin.
Britannica gives Glasgow; other accounts place his death in Dublin during a visit.

people.name: Colin Maclaurin
people.bio: Scottish mathematician who developed and defended Newton's fluxions.

stops.note: Professor of mathematics at Marischal College.
Tour of France as tutor to Lord Polwarth's son.
Fled Edinburgh when the Jacobite army entered it.

people.name: Robert Simson
people.bio: Scottish mathematician, professor of mathematics at Glasgow and editor of Euclid.

people.name: David Hume
people.bio: Scottish philosopher, historian and essayist of the Enlightenment.

stops.note: Attended from about age 11 and left at 15 (c. 1722–26 rather than 1723–25).
Wrote A Treatise of Human Nature.

people.name: Giovanni Battista Morgagni
people.bio: Italian anatomist, founder of pathological anatomy, professor at Padua for sixty years.

stops.note: Graduated in philosophy and medicine 1701; assisted Valsalva.
Theoretical medicine from 1711; first chair of anatomy from 1715/16 until death.

people.name: Antonio Maria Valsalva
people.bio: Italian anatomist at Bologna, pupil of Malpighi, known for his work on the ear.

people.name: Ippolito Francesco Albertini
people.bio: Italian physician and professor of medicine at Bologna, pupil of Malpighi.

people.name: Benito Jerónimo Feijoo
people.bio: Spanish Benedictine monk and essayist, author of the Teatro crítico universal.

stops.note: Taught philosophy and theology at the university.

people.name: Daniel Bernoulli
people.bio: Swiss mathematician and physicist, author of Hydrodynamica.

stops.note: Returned 1734; anatomy and botany, then physiology (1743) and physics (1750–76).

people.name: Immanuel Kant
people.bio: German philosopher of the critical philosophy, professor at Königsberg.

stops.note: Studied at the Albertina; favourite teacher Martin Knutzen.
House tutor outside Königsberg for about six years.
Privatdozent from 1755; professor of logic and metaphysics 1770; retired 1796.

people.name: Martin Knutzen
people.bio: German philosopher and professor of logic and metaphysics at Königsberg, Kant's teacher.

people.name: Joseph-Louis Lagrange
people.bio: Italian-French mathematician of analytical mechanics and the calculus of variations.

stops.note: College of Turin; drawn to physics by Beccaria.
Professor of mathematics at the Royal Artillery School.
Director of mathematics at the Berlin Academy, succeeding Euler.

people.name: Giovanni Battista Beccaria
people.bio: Italian physicist who taught experimental physics at Turin and studied electricity.

people.name: Pierre-Simon Laplace
people.bio: French mathematician and astronomer of celestial mechanics and probability.

stops.note: Theology; teachers Gadbled and Le Canu; left without a degree.
Professor of mathematics at the École Militaire, with d'Alembert's help.
Lectured on probability at the École normale.
Minister of the Interior for about six weeks; later senator and chancellor of the Senate.

people.name: Jean le Rond d'Alembert
people.bio: French mathematician and philosopher, co-editor of the Encyclopédie.

people.name: Christophe Gadbled
people.bio: French mathematician and professor at the University of Caen.

people.name: Gaspard Monge
people.bio: French mathematician, inventor of descriptive geometry and a founder of the École polytechnique.

stops.note: Draughtsman 1765, professor 1769, physics instructor 1770; resigned December 1784.
Helped found the school; taught descriptive geometry.
Egyptian expedition; president of the Institut d'Égypte.

people.name: Johann Lorenz von Mosheim
people.bio: German Lutheran church historian, first chancellor of Göttingen University.

people.name: Anders Celsius
people.bio: Swedish astronomer who devised the centigrade temperature scale and founded the Uppsala observatory.

stops.note: Assisted Eustachio Manfredi; then visited Rome.
French Lapland expedition to measure a degree of the meridian.

people.name: Erik Burman
people.bio: Swedish astronomer and professor at Uppsala.

people.name: Laura Bassi
people.bio: Italian physicist, the second woman to earn a university doctorate and the first to hold a university chair in physics.

stops.note: Doctorate in philosophy May 1732, then reader in philosophy.

people.name: Gaetano Tacconi
people.bio: Bolognese physician and professor who privately tutored Laura Bassi.

people.name: Thomas Reid
people.bio: Scottish philosopher, founder of the common sense school.

stops.note: Studied at Aberdeen under George Turnbull.
Professor (regent) at King's College; SEP dates the appointment to 1752.

people.name: George Turnbull
people.bio: Scottish philosopher and regent at Marischal College, Aberdeen.

people.name: Johann Georg Hamann
people.bio: German Counter-Enlightenment thinker, the 'Magus of the North'.

stops.note: Philosophy and theology, then law; left without a degree.
Business mission for the Berens firm; religious conversion.
Lived in his father's house; minor tax-office post obtained with Kant's help.

people.name: Johann Gottfried Herder
people.bio: German philosopher of language, history and culture.

stops.note: General Superintendent of the Lutheran clergy.

people.name: Johann Gottlieb Fichte
people.bio: German idealist philosopher of the Wissenschaftslehre, first elected rector of Berlin University.

stops.note: After Schulpforta, studied at Jena and Leipzig.
Professor; left after the atheism controversy.
With the Prussian government in exile.
Dean of philosophy and first elected rector.

people.name: G. W. F. Hegel
people.bio: German idealist philosopher, author of the Phenomenology of Spirit.

stops.note: Philosophy and theology at the Stift, with Hölderlin and Schelling.

people.name: F. W. J. Schelling
people.bio: German idealist philosopher of nature and identity.

people.name: Friedrich Schleiermacher
people.bio: German theologian and philosopher, founder of modern hermeneutics.

people.name: Karl Leonhard Reinhold
people.bio: Austrian philosopher who popularized Kant's critical philosophy.

stops.note: Jesuit, then Barnabite seminary; Barnabite priest and teacher.
Fled the order and converted to Protestantism.
First chair devoted to the critical philosophy.

people.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
people.bio: German mathematician and astronomer, director of the Göttingen observatory.

stops.note: Collegium Carolinum on a ducal stipend.
Doctorate on the fundamental theorem of algebra.
Director of the observatory and professor.

people.name: Johann Friedrich Pfaff
people.bio: German mathematician, professor at Helmstedt and Halle.

people.name: Abraham Gotthelf Kästner
people.bio: German mathematician and epigrammatist, professor at Göttingen.

people.name: Martin Bartels
people.bio: German mathematician, later professor at Kazan and Dorpat, teacher of Lobachevsky.

people.name: Joseph Fourier
people.bio: French mathematician and physicist of heat conduction and Fourier series.

stops.note: Chair of analysis and mechanics from 1797.
Egyptian expedition; secretary of the Institut d'Égypte.
Académie des sciences from 1817, secretary from 1822.

people.name: Siméon Denis Poisson
people.bio: French mathematician and physicist of probability, mechanics and potential theory.

stops.note: Chair of mechanics at the new Faculté des sciences; also Bureau des longitudes from 1808.

people.name: Ruggero Giuseppe Boscovich
people.bio: Ragusan Jesuit mathematician, astronomer and natural philosopher.

stops.note: Jesuit novitiate and studies at the Collegio Romano.
Director of the Brera observatory; taught at the Palatine Schools from 1769.
Director of Optics for the French Navy.

people.name: Paolo Ruffini
people.bio: Italian mathematician and physician who gave an early proof that the quintic is not solvable by radicals.

stops.note: Lost his chair in 1798 after refusing the Cisalpine oath.
Taught applied mathematics at the military school.
Rector from 1814; professor of clinical medicine until 1819.

people.name: Paolo Cassiani
people.bio: Italian mathematician, professor at Modena.

people.name: Luigi Fantini
people.bio: Professor of geometry at Modena in the 1780s.

people.name: Carl Linnaeus
people.bio: Swedish botanist and physician who established binomial nomenclature.

stops.note: Lodged with Olof Celsius; made botany teaching assistant by Olof Rudbeck the Younger.
Enrolled at Leiden; Systema Naturae published 1735.
Professor of medicine and botany; ennobled 1761.

people.name: Olof Rudbeck the Younger
people.bio: Swedish naturalist and professor of medicine at Uppsala.

people.name: Olof Celsius
people.bio: Swedish theologian and botanist at Uppsala, uncle of Anders Celsius.

people.name: Johan Stensson Rothman
people.bio: Swedish physician and teacher at Växjö who encouraged Linnaeus to study medicine.

people.name: Albrecht von Haller
people.bio: Swiss physiologist, botanist and poet, professor at Göttingen.

stops.note: Professor of medicine, anatomy, surgery and botany.
Research, medical practice and writing after resigning his chair.

people.name: Joseph Black
people.bio: Scottish chemist who discovered 'fixed air' (carbon dioxide) and latent heat.

stops.note: Medicine; assistant to William Cullen. Entered c. 1744, not 1746.
Succeeded Cullen in chemistry (some sources add the chair of medicine).

people.name: William Cullen
people.bio: Scottish physician and chemist, professor at Glasgow and Edinburgh.

people.name: James Watt
people.bio: Scottish engineer whose separate condenser transformed the steam engine.

stops.note: Apprenticed to a mathematical instrument maker.
Mathematical instrument maker to the university; repaired the Newcomen engine model 1763–64.

people.name: Adam Ferguson
people.bio: Scottish philosopher and historian of civil society.

stops.note: Deputy chaplain to the Black Watch.
Keeper of the Advocates' Library, succeeding Hume.
Secretary to the Carlisle peace commission.

people.name: Dugald Stewart
people.bio: Scottish philosopher of the common sense school, professor at Edinburgh.

stops.note: Taught from age 19; succeeded his father in mathematics 1775.
Professor of moral philosophy, nominally until 1820 (active teaching to about 1810).

people.name: Adam Smith
people.bio: Scottish moral philosopher and political economist, author of The Wealth of Nations.

stops.note: Public lectures on rhetoric and belles-lettres.
Tour of France and Switzerland as tutor to the Duke of Buccleuch.
Worked on The Wealth of Nations.

people.name: Joseph Priestley
people.bio: English dissenting minister, theologian and chemist who isolated oxygen.

stops.note: Daventry Academy, successor of Doddridge's Northampton Academy.
Tutor in languages and belles lettres.
Librarian and companion to Lord Shelburne.
Minister of the New Meeting; home destroyed by rioters 1791.
Taught natural philosophy at the dissenting academy.

people.name: Caleb Ashworth
people.bio: English dissenting minister, head of Daventry Academy after Doddridge.

people.name: Richard Price
people.bio: Welsh dissenting minister, moral philosopher and writer on finance and liberty.

stops.note: Co-founder of New College, Hackney (1786) and on its staff.

people.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
people.bio: German poet, dramatist, novelist, statesman and naturalist.

stops.note: Law; drawing with A. F. Oeser.
A few months at the imperial court of justice.
Privy councillor to Duke Carl August from 1776.

people.name: Adam Friedrich Oeser
people.bio: German painter and director of the Leipzig drawing academy.

people.name: Friedrich Schiller
people.bio: German poet, dramatist, historian and philosopher.

stops.note: Fled Württemberg; resident dramatist at the Mannheim theatre 1783–84.

people.name: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
people.bio: German dramatist, critic and leading writer of the German Enlightenment.

stops.note: Freelance writer and critic; at Wittenberg 1752.

people.name: Edmund Burke
people.bio: Irish-born statesman and political philosopher, critic of the French Revolution.

stops.note: Member of the House of Commons.

people.name: Charles Hutton
people.bio: English mathematician, professor at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich.

people.name: Lorenzo Mascheroni
people.bio: Italian mathematician and priest, known for compass-only constructions.

stops.note: Seminary: rhetoric, then physics and mathematics from 1778.
Professor of algebra and geometry; rector from 1789.
Sent to study the metric system; unable to return.

people.name: Giuseppe Piazzi
people.bio: Italian Theatine astronomer who discovered Ceres, the first asteroid.

stops.note: Theology under Le Seur and Jacquier.
Professor of mathematics, then astronomy; founded the observatory (1790).
Oversaw the Capodimonte observatory; settled in Naples 1824.

people.name: François Jacquier
people.bio: French Minim mathematician in Rome, co-editor of Newton's Principia.

people.name: Lazare Carnot
people.bio: French mathematician, military engineer and revolutionary statesman, 'organizer of victory'.

stops.note: Engineer officer; captain in the Corps royal du génie.
Legislative Assembly, Convention, Committee of Public Safety; Director 1795.
Fled after the coup of Fructidor.
Exiled after Waterloo, first to Warsaw.

people.name: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb
people.bio: French military engineer and physicist, known for the law of electrostatic force.

stops.note: École du génie, taught by Bossut.

people.name: Charles Bossut
people.bio: French mathematician, professor at the engineering school of Mézières.

people.name: John Dalton
people.bio: English Quaker chemist and meteorologist who formulated modern atomic theory.

stops.note: Assistant, later co-principal, at a Quaker boarding school.
Professor of mathematics and natural philosophy at New College (some sources date the start to 1792).
Private mathematical academy; Literary and Philosophical Society (president from 1817).

people.name: John Gough
people.bio: Blind English Quaker natural philosopher of Kendal, Dalton's teacher.

people.name: Elihu Robinson
people.bio: Cumberland Quaker gentleman and naturalist who encouraged the young Dalton.

people.name: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac
people.bio: French chemist and physicist known for the laws of gases.

stops.note: European journey with Alexander von Humboldt.
Professor of physics at the Faculty of Sciences.
Chair of general chemistry at the Muséum.

people.name: Claude-Louis Berthollet
people.bio: Savoyard-French chemist, founder of the Society of Arcueil.

people.name: Wilhelm von Humboldt
people.bio: Prussian philosopher, linguist and statesman who shaped the University of Berlin.

stops.note: Prussian envoy to the Holy See.
Head of the education section; founded the University of Berlin.

people.name: Lazzaro Spallanzani
people.bio: Italian priest and experimental biologist who refuted spontaneous generation.

stops.note: Law, then doctorate in philosophy; cousin Laura Bassi taught there.

people.name: Georg Christoph Lichtenberg
people.bio: German experimental physicist and aphorist, professor at Göttingen.

people.name: Pieter van Musschenbroek
people.bio: Dutch Newtonian physicist, inventor of the Leyden jar.

people.name: Friedrich August Wolf
people.bio: German classical philologist, founder of modern Altertumswissenschaft.

people.name: Abraham Gottlob Werner
people.bio: German mineralogist and Neptunist geologist, teacher at Freiberg.

stops.note: Britannica gives 25 September 1750; 1749 is usual elsewhere.
Inspector and teacher at the mining academy for some forty years.

people.name: Antoine-Laurent de Jussieu
people.bio: French botanist who devised the natural system of plant classification.

stops.note: Botany demonstrator from 1770; helped organize the Muséum in 1790; professor until 1826.

people.name: Bernard de Jussieu
people.bio: French botanist at the Jardin du Roi, uncle of Antoine-Laurent de Jussieu.

people.name: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
people.bio: French naturalist, pioneer of evolutionary theory and invertebrate zoology.

stops.note: Professor at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle.

people.name: Luigi Galvani
people.bio: Italian physician and anatomist who discovered 'animal electricity'.

stops.note: Doctorates in medicine and philosophy, July 1759.
Institute of Sciences from 1761 (anatomy professor 1766, obstetrics 1782); university lectureship from 1768; dismissed April 1798 for refusing the Cisalpine oath.

people.name: Jacopo Bartolomeo Beccari
people.bio: Italian chemist and physician at Bologna.

people.name: Domenico Gusmano Galeazzi
people.bio: Italian anatomist and physician at Bologna, Galvani's teacher and father-in-law.

people.name: Antonio Genovesi
people.bio: Neapolitan priest and philosopher who held Europe's first chair of political economy.

stops.note: Private school from 1739; attended Vico's lectures.
Chair of 'mechanics and commerce' (political economy), funded by Intieri.

people.name: Domenico Vandelli
people.bio: Italian naturalist who founded natural history and chemistry teaching at Coimbra.

stops.note: Botany under Pontedera and Arduino; graduated under Morgagni c. 1761.
Organised the royal botanical garden at Ajuda.
Professor of chemistry and natural history; retired 1791.

people.name: Giulio Pontedera
people.bio: Italian botanist, prefect of the Padua botanical garden.

people.name: Alessandro Volta
people.bio: Italian physicist, inventor of the electric pile.

stops.note: Head of the Gymnasium; professor of experimental physics 1775.
Tour of Switzerland and Alsace; met de Saussure.
Professor of experimental physics from 1778 (briefly removed 1799–1800).
France and England; met Lavoisier and Laplace.
Demonstrated the pile before the Institut and Napoleon.

people.name: Adamantios Korais
people.bio: Greek classical scholar and physician, a central figure of the Modern Greek Enlightenment.

stops.note: Graduated from the Evangelical School (years approximate).

people.name: Gaspar Melchor de Jovellanos
people.bio: Spanish Enlightenment statesman, jurist and writer on agrarian reform.

stops.note: Law studies (also at Oviedo and Ávila); years approximate.
Banished to Asturias; founded an institute for regional reform.
Minister of justice for eight months.

people.name: Joseph-Louis Proust
people.bio: French chemist who formulated the law of definite proportions, working mostly in Spain.

stops.note: Professor of chemistry at the Seminario Patriótico.
Royal artillery school (chair formally from 1792); moved to Madrid 1799.

people.name: Hilaire-Martin Rouelle
people.bio: French chemist who lectured at the Jardin du Roi.

people.name: Walter Scott
people.bio: Scottish novelist and poet, author of the Waverley novels.

stops.note: Sheriff-depute of Selkirkshire; later a clerk of the Court of Session.

people.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
people.bio: German composer and pianist, central to the transition from Classical to Romantic music.

stops.note: Studied with Haydn, Albrechtsberger and Salieri; composer and pianist.

people.name: Christian Gottlob Neefe
people.bio: German composer and court organist at Bonn.

people.name: Joseph Haydn
people.bio: Austrian composer of the Classical period.

people.name: Johann Georg Albrechtsberger
people.bio: Austrian composer, organist and teacher of counterpoint.

people.name: Antonio Salieri
people.bio: Italian composer, Kapellmeister at the Viennese court.

people.name: Klemens von Metternich
people.bio: Austrian foreign minister and chancellor, architect of the post-Napoleonic order.

stops.note: Foreign minister; chancellor from 1821; host of the Congress of Vienna.

people.name: Heinrich von Kleist
people.bio: German dramatist and novella writer.

people.name: Karl Friedrich Schinkel
people.bio: Prussian architect and painter of Neoclassicism and Gothic Revival.

stops.note: Several years in Italy; returned via Paris 1805.
State architect of Prussia; head of the Office of Public Works from 1830.

people.name: Friedrich Gilly
people.bio: German Neoclassical architect and teacher at the Berlin Bauakademie.

people.name: August Wilhelm Schlegel
people.bio: German critic, translator of Shakespeare and pioneer of Sanskrit studies.

stops.note: Tutor in Madame de Staël's household.
Professor of literature and art history.

people.name: Hans Christian Ørsted
people.bio: Danish physicist and chemist who discovered electromagnetism.

stops.note: Travels in the German lands and France.

people.name: Friedrich Carl von Savigny
people.bio: German jurist, founder of the historical school of law.

stops.note: Study tour of France and southern Germany.

people.name: Thomas Chalmers
people.bio: Scottish minister and theologian, first moderator of the Free Church of Scotland.

stops.note: Entered aged about 11; licensed to preach 1799.
Tron parish, then St John's from 1819.
Principal of the Free Church's New College.

people.name: William Hazlitt
people.bio: English essayist and critic.

people.name: Novalis
people.bio: German Romantic poet and philosopher (Friedrich von Hardenberg).

people.name: Friedrich Hölderlin
people.bio: German lyric poet and philosopher of German Idealism's circle.

stops.note: Lived in the tower on the Neckar.

people.name: Esaias Tegnér
people.bio: Swedish poet, professor of Greek at Lund and bishop of Växjö.

people.name: George Birkbeck
people.bio: English physician and pioneer of adult education for working men.

stops.note: Professor of natural philosophy; lectures for artisans.
Co-founder and president of the London Mechanics' Institution.

people.name: Mikhail Lomonosov
people.bio: Russian polymath, chemist and poet, co-founder of Moscow University.

stops.note: Scholarship to the Academy, then sent abroad.
Academy of Sciences: adjunct 1742, professor of chemistry 1745.

people.name: Johann Friedrich Henckel
people.bio: German physician, mineralogist and mining official at Freiberg.

people.name: Gerard van Swieten
people.bio: Dutch-Austrian physician who reformed medical education in the Habsburg lands.

stops.note: Medical practice and private pharmacy courses (banned 1734).
Physician to Maria Theresa; reformed the Vienna medical faculty from 1749.

people.name: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus
people.bio: German-Dutch anatomist, professor at Leiden.

people.name: Petrus Camper
people.bio: Dutch anatomist, naturalist and physician.

stops.note: Degrees in medicine and philosophy c. 1746.
Anatomy and surgery at the Athenaeum Illustre.

people.name: Willem 's Gravesande
people.bio: Dutch Newtonian natural philosopher and mathematician, professor at Leiden.

people.name: Alexander Monro primus
people.bio: Scottish anatomist who founded the Edinburgh medical school's anatomy teaching.

stops.note: Professor of anatomy 1720 (university chair 1725) until resignation in 1764, not 1758.

people.name: William Cheselden
people.bio: English surgeon and anatomist in London.

people.name: Alexander Gottlieb Baumgarten
people.bio: German Wolffian philosopher who named and founded aesthetics as a discipline.

stops.note: Doctorate 1735; heard Wolffian lectures at Jena in 1733.

people.name: Johann Peter Reusch
people.bio: German Wolffian philosopher and professor at Jena.

people.name: Georg Friedrich Meier
people.bio: German philosopher at Halle, populariser of Baumgarten's aesthetics.

people.name: Gregorio Mayans
people.bio: Spanish Enlightenment jurist, historian and philologist.

stops.note: Law under Tosca, Corachán and Íñigo.
Royal librarian for about seven years.

people.name: Tomás Vicente Tosca
people.bio: Spanish Oratorian mathematician and philosopher of the Valencian novatores.

people.name: Manuel Martí
people.bio: Spanish humanist, dean of Alicante.

people.name: Vasily Trediakovsky
people.bio: Russian poet and theorist who reformed Russian versification.

people.name: Diego de Torres Villarroel
people.bio: Spanish writer, almanac-maker and professor of mathematics at Salamanca.

stops.note: Later graduated in medicine at Ávila.
Professor of mathematics; retired on a pension in 1750 (not 1751).

people.name: Hermann Samuel Reimarus
people.bio: German deist philosopher and orientalist whose critique of the Bible Lessing published.

stops.note: Professor of Hebrew and oriental languages at the Akademisches Gymnasium.

people.name: Johann Albert Fabricius
people.bio: German classical bibliographer and professor at the Hamburg Gymnasium.

people.name: Jorge Juan
people.bio: Spanish naval officer, mathematician and scientist of the equatorial geodesic mission.

stops.note: Page to the Grand Master of Malta.
Royal Company of Marine Guards (1730 rather than 1729).
French geodesic mission to the equator, with Antonio de Ulloa.
Captain of the Royal Company of Marine Guards.
Ambassador to the Sultan of Morocco.
Director of the Seminary of Nobles.

people.name: Georges-Louis Leclerc, comte de Buffon
people.bio: French naturalist, author of the Histoire naturelle and intendant of the Jardin du Roi.

stops.note: Jesuit Collège des Godrans, then law.
With the Duke of Kingston through southern France and Italy.
Intendant of the Jardin du Roi; Histoire naturelle from 1749.

people.name: Horace-Bénédict de Saussure
people.bio: Genevan physicist and Alpine geologist, pioneer of mountaineering science.

stops.note: Professor of physics and philosophy at the Academy.

people.name: Philip Doddridge
people.bio: English Nonconformist minister, hymn writer and head of the Northampton dissenting academy.

stops.note: Head of the new academy, moved to Northampton in 1729.
Academy head and pastor of the independent congregation.

people.name: John Jennings
people.bio: English dissenting tutor at Kibworth, Leicestershire.

people.name: Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach
people.bio: German composer and keyboard player at the Prussian court and in Hamburg.

people.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
people.bio: German Baroque composer, Thomaskantor in Leipzig.

people.name: Hryhorii Skovoroda
people.bio: Ukrainian philosopher, poet and teacher, a wandering sage.

stops.note: With the Tokaj wine commission in Hungary and Central Europe.

people.name: Eugenios Voulgaris
people.bio: Greek scholar and cleric of the Modern Greek Enlightenment, later archbishop in Russia.

stops.note: Temporary head of the Patriarchal Academy.

people.name: Iosipos Moisiodax
people.bio: Aromanian-Greek Enlightenment scholar, director of the Princely Academy of Iași.

stops.note: Director 1765–66, interrupted by a decade in Wallachia, briefly again before 1777.

people.name: Oliver Goldsmith
people.bio: Irish novelist, playwright and poet.

people.name: Anders Chydenius
people.bio: Finnish-Swedish priest and liberal economist, champion of press freedom.

stops.note: Royal Academy of Åbo; also studied at Uppsala.
Member of the Riksdag; Freedom of the Press Act.

people.name: Pehr Kalm
people.bio: Swedish-Finnish naturalist, Linnaeus's pupil, known for his North American travels.

stops.note: Field research in Sweden, Russia and Ukraine.

people.name: Jean-Rodolphe Perronet
people.bio: French civil engineer and bridge builder, founding head of the École des ponts et chaussées.

stops.note: Directed the training school (named École des ponts et chaussées 1775).

people.name: Pedro Virgili
people.bio: Catalan military surgeon who founded Spain's royal colleges of surgery.

stops.note: Founded the Royal College of Surgery (source dates the foundation inconsistently).

people.name: Robert Joseph Pothier
people.bio: French jurist whose treatises shaped the Napoleonic Code.

people.name: Christian Gottlob Heyne
people.bio: German classical philologist and librarian at Göttingen.

stops.note: Professor of classics and director of the library.

people.name: Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin
people.bio: Dutch-Austrian botanist and chemist, professor at Vienna.

stops.note: Medicine; then Paris, attending Antoine de Jussieu's lectures.
Professor of botany and chemistry; director of the botanical garden.

people.name: Georges Cuvier
people.bio: French naturalist, founder of comparative anatomy and palaeontology.

stops.note: Assistant to Mertrud at the Jardin des Plantes, then professor.
Succeeded Daubenton in natural history in 1799 (not 1800).

people.name: Carl Friedrich Kielmeyer
people.bio: German naturalist and teacher at the Karlsschule and Tübingen.

people.name: Alexander von Humboldt
people.bio: Prussian naturalist and explorer, author of Kosmos.

people.name: Jöns Jacob Berzelius
people.bio: Swedish chemist, a founder of modern chemistry.

stops.note: Professor of chemistry and pharmacy from 1807 (the Karolinska Institute was formally founded 1810).

people.name: Anders Gustaf Ekeberg
people.bio: Swedish chemist at Uppsala, discoverer of tantalum.

people.name: Johan Afzelius
people.bio: Swedish chemist, professor at Uppsala.

people.name: Samuel Thomas Soemmerring
people.bio: German anatomist, physiologist and inventor.

stops.note: Professor of anatomy at the Collegium Carolinum.
Dean of medicine for five years; left after the French annexation (c. 1795, not 1797).

people.name: Ernst Gottfried Baldinger
people.bio: German physician, professor at Göttingen and Marburg.

people.name: Jan Śniadecki
people.bio: Polish mathematician, astronomer and philosopher, rector of Vilnius University.

stops.note: Taught astronomy; director of the Kraków observatory.

people.name: Marcin Poczobutt
people.bio: Lithuanian Jesuit astronomer, director of the Vilnius observatory and rector of the university.

stops.note: Worked at the Marseille observatory under Pézenas.

people.name: Esprit Pézenas
people.bio: French Jesuit astronomer at the Marseille observatory.

people.name: Hugo Kołłątaj
people.bio: Polish priest, reformer of Kraków University and co-author of the Constitution of 3 May.

stops.note: Studied in Vienna, Naples and Rome.

people.name: Adam Weishaupt
people.bio: German law professor at Ingolstadt and founder of the Bavarian Illuminati.

stops.note: Law, canon law from 1773; lost the post in 1784 (not 1785).
Under the patronage of Duke Ernest II.

people.name: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
people.bio: Austrian orientalist and diplomat, first president of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

stops.note: Educated mainly in Vienna (Oriental Academy) before entering diplomatic service in 1796.
Austrian embassy; took part in the campaign against the French in Egypt.

people.name: Johann Michael Sailer
people.bio: German Catholic theologian and educator, bishop of Regensburg.

stops.note: Studies, then tutor (1777) and professor of dogmatics (1780).

people.name: James Beattie
people.bio: Scottish poet and common-sense moral philosopher.

people.name: Henrik Gabriel Porthan
people.bio: Finnish historian and humanist, father of Finnish historiography.

people.name: Kosmas the Aetolian
people.bio: Greek Orthodox monk and missionary preacher who founded many schools.

stops.note: Attended the Athonite Academy as a monk.

people.name: Giovanni Poleni
people.bio: Italian mathematician and physicist at Padua.

people.name: Fausto Elhuyar
people.bio: Spanish chemist and mining engineer, co-discoverer of tungsten.

stops.note: Professor of mineralogy and metallurgy; tungsten isolated 1783.
Director-general of mines; first director of the School of Mines.

people.name: José Bonifácio de Andrada e Silva
people.bio: Brazilian mineralogist and statesman, 'Patriarch of Independence'.

stops.note: Chemistry and mineralogy in Europe; discovered petalite.
Professor of geology; Lisbon Academy secretary 1812.

people.name: José María Blanco White
people.bio: Spanish-born priest, poet and journalist who settled in England.

people.name: Eulogius Schneider
people.bio: German Franciscan, professor at Bonn and Jacobin in Strasbourg, guillotined.

stops.note: Franciscan from 1777 (Bamberg); completed studies and ordained.
Court chaplain to Duke Karl Eugen.
Professor of literature and fine arts.

people.name: Franz von Fürstenberg
people.bio: Westphalian statesman and educational reformer, founder of the University of Münster.

stops.note: Jurisprudence; degree at the Sapienza in Rome 1753.
Founded the university (1773 per this source, opened 1780) and was its curator.

people.name: Athanasios Parios
people.bio: Greek Orthodox theologian and teacher, head of the School of Chios.

people.name: Athanasios Psalidas
people.bio: Greek scholar of the Modern Greek Enlightenment, head of the Kaplaneios School in Ioannina.

stops.note: Director for about 25 years after returning in 1796.

people.name: Christoph Traugott Delius
people.bio: German-Austrian mining scientist, professor at Schemnitz and author of a standard mining textbook.

stops.note: Court councillor for mining and minting.

people.name: Josep Finestres
people.bio: Catalan jurist and humanist, leading professor of the University of Cervera.

stops.note: Doctorate 1715, then successive law chairs; prime chair from 1751 (teaching from 1715, not 1734).

people.name: Antonio de Gimbernat
people.bio: Catalan anatomist and surgeon, known for work on hernia; director of the San Carlos college in Madrid.

stops.note: Paris, London (demonstrated to John Hunter's class 1777), Edinburgh, Leiden, Amsterdam.

people.name: Mihály Csokonai Vitéz
people.bio: Hungarian poet of the Enlightenment.

stops.note: Taught the poetry class from 1794; dismissed 1795.

people.name: Makarios Kalogeras
people.bio: Greek Orthodox deacon and teacher, founder of the Patmian School.

stops.note: Theology and philosophy at the Patriarchal School.
Founded and taught at the Patmian School.

people.name: Gerasimos Byzantios
people.bio: Greek teacher, pupil and successor of Makarios Kalogeras at the Patmian School.

people.name: Neophytos Kafsokalyvitis
people.bio: Greek Orthodox monk and teacher, first head of the Athonite Academy.

stops.note: Under Gerasimos Byzantios; also studied in Constantinople and Ioannina.
Led the school from its founding (1748, not 1749) until replaced by Voulgaris.
